---
title: "Usage and examples"
subtitle: "Every form of metest, from the help file, with output"
---
<<dd_version: 2>>

```stata
metest [exp] [, options]
```

*exp* refers to marginal effects by the `#` shown in the `mecompare` table,
or by their coefficient names, combined with `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, parentheses,
or `=`. A bare number is always an ME number; a literal number is written
with a leading `#` (`#2` is the number two, `2` is the second marginal
effect). Non-whole numbers are always literals.

The examples below are the ones in the [help file](help.html), run in order.

## Setup: fit and store two models, then calculate the marginal effects

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
sysuse nlsw88, clear
drop if missing(union, married, age, race, wage)

logit union i.married age i.race, vce(robust)
est store m1
logit union i.married age i.race wage, vce(robust)
est store m2

mecompare age i.married, models(m1 m2)
<</dd_do>>
```

## A single marginal effect, by number and by name

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
metest 1
metest age:m1
<</dd_do>>
```

## The cross-model difference, three equivalent ways

Note that `mecompare` already reports it as ME 3.

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
metest 1 - 2
metest 3
metest _b[age:m1] - _b[age:m2]
<</dd_do>>
```

## A ratio and an average

Note the `#` on the divisor of the average, which makes it the number two rather
than ME 2.

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
metest 1 / 2
metest (1 + 2) / #2
<</dd_do>>
```

## Scaling by a literal value

10 times the effect for a change in age:

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
metest 1 * #10
<</dd_do>>
```

## Equality tests, including a joint test and two constraints at once

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
metest 1 = 2
metest 1 = 2 = 3
metest (1 = 2) (4 = 5)
<</dd_do>>
```

## Building up a table

Estimates and equality tests are shown in separate tables.

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
metest, clear
metest 1 - 2
metest 4 - 5, add
metest 1 = 2, add
<</dd_do>>
```

Redisplayed at any point, with a title, by typing `metest` on its own:

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
metest, title("Age and marriage")
<</dd_do>>
```

## All six statistics, and a label of your own

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
metest 1 - 2, stat(all)
metest 1 - 2, rowname("Age effect, m1 vs m2")
<</dd_do>>
```

## Options

| Option | Purpose |
|:--|:--|
| `statistics(list)` | Statistics to display: `estimate`, `se`, `zvalue`, `pvalue`, `ll`, `ul`, or `all`. The default is `estimate se pvalue`. Ignored for equality tests, which report the test statistic, its degrees of freedom, and the p-value. `stats()` is a synonym. |
| `allstats` | Same as `statistics(all)`. |
| `add` | Adds the result as another row of the saved table rather than starting a new one. `save` is a synonym. |
| `clear` | Clears the saved table before running; `metest, clear` on its own clears it without running anything. |
| `rowname(string)` | Labels the row. A `:` in the label puts what comes before it on a row of its own, with the rest indented underneath, which is how several rows are grouped under one heading. `label()` is a synonym. |
| `decimals(#)` | Decimal places; the default is 3. |
| `width(#)` | Width of each statistic column; the default is 9. |
| `labwidth(#)` | Width of the label column; the maximum is 32. `twidth()` is a synonym. |
| `title(string)` | Title above the table. |
| `notable` | Suppresses the table. |
| `details` | Shows the underlying `nlcom` or `test` output. |
| `level(#)` | Confidence level for `ll` and `ul`. |

Results accumulate in the matrix `_metest` (estimates) and `_metest_test`
(equality tests). `metest` is r-class: after an expression it returns
`r(estimate)`, `r(se)`, `r(zvalue)`, `r(pvalue)`, `r(ll)`, and `r(ul)`; after
an equality test, `r(chi2)` (or `r(F)`), `r(df)`, and `r(pvalue)`.

## Use after other commands

`metest` also works after other estimation commands: a number refers to the
*n*th coefficient in `e(b)`, in the order of `matrix list e(b)`, and
coefficient names work as usual.

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
sysuse nlsw88, clear
regress wage age ttl_exp grade
metest 1 - 2
metest 1 / 2
metest 1 = 2 = 3
metest abs(1) - abs(2)
metest min(1,2)
metest _b[age] * #10
<</dd_do>>
```

After `margins, post`, a number refers to a row of the `margins` table. E.g.,
a risk ratio -- the ratio of two predicted probabilities, averaging over
observed values -- in the Health and Retirement Study 2020:

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
use "https://tdmize.github.io/data/data/cda_hrs", clear
drop if missing(cogB, marstatB, collegeB, woman, age)

logit cogB i.collegeB i.marstatB i.woman c.age, or

margins collegeB, post
metest 1 / 2
<</dd_do>>
```

Omitted (`o.`) coefficients are skipped when numbering, so check the numbers
with `matrix list e(b)`. After some commands `test` reports *F* rather than
chi-squared; run `metest, clear` before accumulating results from a model of
the other kind.
